correctness.rationale: The constant, partner-antisymmetric, and mean-zero partner-symmetric spaces have eigenvalues 0, N−2, and N. The spectral resolution gives only one possibly negative entry in each row, −F/(2N), with row sum one, proving both induced norms. The stated sign vector is an ℓ∞ extremizer; a basis vector is an ℓ1 extremizer. The sign of F′ is the sign of (N/(N−2))^(s−1) exp(−(N^s−(N−2)^s)t)−1; this gives the unique peak and positive recovery root for s>1 and no negative entries for s≤1. In u=N^s t the locally uniform limit of F is 2[(1+su)exp(−u)−1], and sign bracketing traps the unique positive root. With s=1+δ and t=δv, the limit of F/δ² is N(N−2)v(r_N−v), giving the cutoff and, with the exact peak time, the quadratic amplitude. At high powers, the peak separates the two decay scales and F at fixed v=(N−2)^s t>0 tends to N exp(−v)−2. The finite-power bound is strict at the attained peak. No numerical step is needed.
residual_risks: The frozen assertion count is recorded, not an independent replay. Fractional tests use the closed kernel; Taylor comparisons independently test integer powers at the indicated finite times. The analytic reconstruction supplies the all-parameter check.
The sign-function statement is read as concerning the immediately preceding ℓ∞ norm, not ℓ1.
